messages:
ryan_sales: Hey team — Hawthorne Health is greenlighting a Private deployment POC. They want a runbook for network handoff: preserve client IP, minimal egress allowlist, DNS resolution, and a sample test plan. Can ops/SE confirm the simplest path?
joanne_se: Congrats! Quick Q: will customer route via PrivateLink (interface endpoint) or TGW with peering? They indicated an on-prem MPLS to AWS transit/router.
sam_netops: They said PrivateLink preferred to avoid peering complexity. That means interface endpoints in the customer VPC and traffic egress from our VPC -> customer via endpoint. We need customer to allow inbound to the endpoint ENIs.
ryan_sales: Right — they requested a short allowlist we can give their infra team plus a curl test for verification.
elaine_security: Also add required egress ports for heartbeat/metrics to our control plane and KMS if they opt for CMK. Need explicit IP ranges for compliance.
andy_eng: Minimal items from runtime side: 1) outbound TLS to control plane (443) to these CIDRs, 2) option for outbound to S3 for model artifacts (if using on-demand pulls), 3) if using Private deployment with VPC endpoints, customer must allow traffic to our interface endpoint ENIs.
sam_netops: Draft allowlist snippet below (customer to apply on their firewall / proxy):

```
# Allowlist for Hawthorne POC (egress from customer to Redwood Private endpoint)
# 1) Control plane endpoints (managed): 34.198.10.0/24, 52.23.180.0/24
# 2) Artifact storage (S3 endpoints) - prefer gateway endpoint; if not, allow 52.216.0.0/15
# 3) TLS for metrics/health checks: outbound 443 to control plane IPs
# 4) DNS: allow UDP/TCP 53 to their resolver and to the VPC resolver (169.254.169.253 if using resolver endpoint)

# Example firewall rules (high level):
ALLOW TCP 443 -> 34.198.10.0/24  # redwood control plane
ALLOW TCP 443 -> <privatelink-interface-ENI-ips>  # runtime endpoints
ALLOW TCP/UDP 53 -> <customer-dns-resolver-ips>
ALLOW TCP 443 -> 52.216.0.0/15  # S3 (if applicable)
```

joanne_se: Can we avoid giving CIDRs for control plane when they require strict allowlist? They need a small set of stable IPs. Do we have a published set we can commit to for the POC?
andy_eng: For short POC we can allocate stable egress IPs from our side and publish them in the runbook. For production we'd recommend PrivateLink + NAT supernets so customer can pin them. I'll follow up with exact IPs (ETA ~1h).
elaine_security: If they request CMK, KMS calls will originate from our control plane IPs — add those to allowlist. Also note: no keys or model content flow through their network unless they opt-in for artifact pulls. Document that for their security team.
ryan_sales: Pricing note from the customer: they asked if PrivateLink adds bandwidth or endpoint charges. I told them we'd share a POC cost estimate. Who can provide a ballpark?
joanne_se: For POC (small traffic) the main costs: PrivateLink endpoint hourly + data transfer (AWS), plus our Private deployment seat. I'll send a simple table after IPs are confirmed.
sam_netops: Test plan (simple):
1) Customer applies firewall allowlist above.
2) On their host, run: curl -v https://<privatelink-fqdn>/health
3) Verify TCP handshake to ENI IP and TLS cert SNI matches expected.
4) Send small inference payload and confirm response and preserved source IP in our logs (we'll share sample logs).

Example debug curl:
```
curl -v -H "Host: private-redwood.example.com" https://<privatelink-fqdn>/health
```

andy_eng: We'll put a simple log snippet in the runbook showing where preserved client IP appears and how to grep for it. Also add a fallback to a regional hosted endpoint in case PrivateLink fails.
elaine_security: One last ask from compliance: they'd like packet capture proof that TLS terminates at our endpoint (no TLS interception). We can provide a pcap from the test or a tcpdump example they can run.
ryan_sales: Great — next steps: @andy_eng provide stable POC IPs, @joanne_se provide cost table, @sam_netops assemble the allowlist + curl test into a single runbook doc to hand to customer. I'll coordinate timing with Hawthorne. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deployment template created: poc/hawthorne/privatedeploy/initial-handsoff (ID: poc-4692)
joanne_se: acked. I'll slot a 30-min handoff call for Thursday 10am PT.
andy_eng: POC stable IPs: 34.210.77.16, 34.210.77.17, control plane 52.25.10.8. Adding KMS egress: 3.231.44.12. I'll update runbook now.
sam_netops: Runbook draft uploaded to the handoff template. Sharing the link with Hawthorne infra in the call.
ryan_sales: Thanks all — I'll attach the runbook to the SOW and update the customer.
elaine_security: I'll be on the call for compliance Qs.
ryan_sales: Closing thread, will post any follow-ups after the handoff call.
